question: Is cheap conditional response ordering already implemented, actually enabled, and equivalent to the Pro-linked mature continuation history?
source_coverage: Upstream move history table/update, continuation offsets, quiet/evasion score, worker reset and call sites; not whole Stockfish correctness or playing evaluation. Own MoveOrderer, StagedMovePicker, negamax/root context, public Player, learner constructor and existing probe/tests read.

current_reuse.producer_hook: negamax beta cutoff invokes record_countermove(prev_action,action) only when use_ordering and non-None previous search-path action
current_reuse.consumer_hook: MoveOrderer/MovePicker only reorder members of actual legal list; TT/capture/promotion precedence can shadow quiet countermove priority
current_reuse.lifecycle: one fresh MoveOrderer per root-search Context; shared across iterative depths, not retained by a persistent Player across choose calls
current_reuse.actual_played_prefix: root negamax starts with previous actionNone; does not seed response context from the last played GameRecord action
current_reuse.learner: maintained mainline_search.search constructs SearchTuning(root tacticalFalse,fullPVTrue) without countermove. Existing feature not used by that caller; no API option added.

upstream_not_equivalent: Stockfish uses multiple previous-ply piece/target contexts, in-check/capture conditioning, signed saturating updates and multiple history/threat/material terms. Generic single previous-fullAction response is a cheap component, not this whole heuristic. No constants/Chess piece priors/SEE/capture or pawn tables ported.

saved_return_observation.source_constructor: all three frozen script constructors pass only localhash tuning; countermove remains defaultFalse. Zero hits alone would not prove disabled or ineffective; frozen source supplies the first conclusion, no effect test supplies the second.

first_opportunity_source_lemma.premises: ordinary fresh root Context, full-window iterative main search, no extra main extensions/research policy, q ordering does not use countermove, no external injected orderer history, distinct public root actions
first_opportunity_source_lemma.if_no_attempt_beyond_D2: No direct countermove priority can be consumed: D1 has root previousNone, D2 child previous keys are unique root actions not yet revisited. Later main iteration/work can create/reuse context. This is not an equal-wall action-equivalence claim.
first_opportunity_source_lemma.caveat: A retained completed_depth2 return may include aborted D3+ work and its hits; use actual work/result_source. Potential D3+ exposure need not be a hit; TT may already prioritize the same response, or the response is not an eligible quiet/legal member.
first_opportunity_source_lemma.not_universal: No rule/game strength prediction or new runtime test is claimed from this source argument.

measurement_limits: countermove_hits counts eligible priority exposure, not necessarily changed rank, cheaper proof, completed result effect or quality. Existing product source says this explicitly.
Current saved data did not enable the feature, so no acceleration/quality/learner benefit follows.
One future comparison must select one declared mechanism and preserve all fixed service/caps; do not add this to the current PRIMARY PN arm or call it a Stockfish port.
decision: REUSE existing opt-in if this exact cheap one-step response mechanism is later selected; do not build a second conditional orderer, model or multi-history system now. Current PRIMARY owns its separate prospective policy experiment. New ordinary AUX work is source-only, zero new Player/PN/Core/game/train/build calls.
